ratings_why.fun: Setting the river each turn (who opens the way, who waits at B1, who catches the Gift) is a fresh puzzle, and Stamps plus Alevin triples give steady growth you can see.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: the board itself is a one-way river and each death moves the whole run up mid-fight, so slot order decides who goes home; no tribe today or in Battlegrounds moves units along a path in the fight.

verdict_why: The v2 readability fixes landed; what's left is wording polish and UI, not a broken or unreadable card.

points.text: Captain Kype's 'it attacks at once' reads against Leap's 'leaping doesn't add an attack'. Saying 'makes an extra attack' marks it as the exception.
Sea Trout Ferrywife's Leap moves with her as the run climbs, so who has Leap changes mid-fight. 'Units alongside this at Start of Combat have Leap this fight' would fix who gets it.
Old Bradán fires every fish's Gift at once at Start of Combat, which is hard to predict from the board. A preview of each Gift's arrows while recruiting would make him readable.
The fantasy lives in the River, so the board should draw it: a current along the zigzag, Stamp pips on every fish and B1 marked as the next pilgrim with its Gift shown.
Pebble-Carrying Hen is a quiet rules tweak; the pebble from your own redd could do more, such as the Alevin keeping the parent's Spent text.

standouts.why: Old Kelt drifts to the mouth and the whole run leaps up behind him: the seed's image and the mechanic are one move.
The Bailiff stamps passports each turn and eats a pilgrim when sold; you can read the heron from the rules alone.
Reunion Cock turns year-classes into a matching puzzle that the run's shared leaping keeps lined up.

weakest.why: Old Bradán's mass replay at Start of Combat is the hardest card to read at a glance.
Pebble-Carrying Hen is a small number change with little play of its own.
Sea Trout Ferrywife's aura shifts as she and her neighbours leap, so who has Leap is hard to track.

flags.note: Old Bradán's in-fight total is about twice the tier guide by the designer's own count.
Mother Redd with the Warden and Little Jack Gravel can make a golden Alevin, and so a Discover, nearly every turn.
